prayerExcerpt.en-US: The soul cannot truly serve God while it is involved in the distractions and pleasures of the world.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: A alma não pode verdadeiramente servir a Deus enquanto está envolvida nas distrações e nos prazeres do mundo.

meta.face: An East Anglian princess of about forty with a fair, clear complexion and a softly PEAR-SHAPED face — NARROW at the temples and widening to FULL lower cheeks and a broad, rounded jaw; a straight nose that continues the line of the forehead in ONE UNBROKEN LINE (a classical profile); LARGE, WIDE-SET, heavy-lidded pale-blue eyes under HIGH, curved fair brows; a SMALL, full, rosebud mouth; a SHORT, rounded chin; the neck plain and unadorned; all hair hidden; the gaze calm and inward.
meta.basis: No likeness survives. The Benedictional of St. Æthelwold (tenth century; Commons) shows her veiled, with a book and a budding staff, and Wikipedia tells the legend of the ash that grew from her staff, and Bede's account of her dying of a neck tumour she took as penance for the necklaces of her youth. The book tells her two marriages kept in virginity, her refuge on a headland near Coldingham, and the double monastery she founded at Ely in 672. The pear-shaped face with the classical profile is our choice.
